*viaimcp.txt*	A Model Context Protocol server for ViAI help and Vim script

Author:  Hirohito Higashi <h.east.727@gmail.com>
License: Vim license, see |license|

==============================================================================
CONTENTS					*viaimcp-contents*

1. Introduction				|viaimcp-introduction|
2. Requirements				|viaimcp-requirements|
3. Setup				|viaimcp-setup|
4. Tools				|viaimcp-tools|
5. Development				|viaimcp-development|

==============================================================================
1. Introduction					*viaimcp-introduction*

viai.mcp is a server of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that gives an AI tool
the help files of ViAI and a check of Vim script.  It is written in Vim9
script and runs in a ViAI of its own, which talks MCP on its stdin and stdout
with the "mcp" channel mode, see |model-context-protocol|.

The answers come from that ViAI: its help files, the help files of the
plugins on the 'runtimepath' it is given, see |viaimcp-runtimepath|, and
what it reports when it reads a script.

==============================================================================
2. Requirements					*viaimcp-requirements*

ViAI 1.0.0050 or later, which has the "mcp" channel mode.  Vim itself does
not have it.

==============================================================================
3. Setup					*viaimcp-setup*

Put viai.mcp on 'runtimepath' for this help and |viaimcp#Command()|, with a
plugin manager, vim-plug for instance: >
	Plug 'viai-editor/viai.mcp'
<There is no plugin/ directory in it, so ViAI runs none of it at startup.

The server is started by the MCP client.  The command is in bin/: >
	bin/viaimcp		(Unix)
	bin\viaimcp.cmd		(MS-Windows)
<It runs "viai" from $PATH; $VIAIMCP_VIM names another ViAI.

For Claude Code: >
	claude mcp add viaimcp -- /path/to/viai.mcp/bin/viaimcp
<
						*viaimcp#Command()*
viaimcp#Command()
		Returns the command that starts the server as a |List|: the
		console program of this ViAI with "--clean", "--stdio-channel",
		the 'runtimepath' of this ViAI, see |viaimcp-runtimepath|, and
		"-S" with the script of the server.  Throws an error when this
		is not ViAI 1.0.0050 or later.

						*viaimcp-runtimepath*
The server is started with "--clean", which reads no vimrc and no plugin,
thus the plugins of the user are not on 'runtimepath'.  The environment
variable $VIAIMCP_RUNTIMEPATH gives the 'runtimepath' to use: the help files
of the plugins on it are found and so are the scripts that a checked script
imports by name.  Nothing on it is run.  The help files of the ViAI of the
server are always found.

Get the value from your ViAI with your vimrc, for Claude Code on Unix: >
	claude mcp add viaimcp \
		-e VIAIMCP_RUNTIMEPATH="$(viai -u ~/.vimrc -i NONE -es \
		-c 'call writefile([&rtp], "/dev/stdout")' -c 'qa!')" \
		-- /path/to/viai.mcp/bin/viaimcp
<"-es" reads no vimrc, thus "-u" names it.  After changing the plugins, run
"claude mcp remove viaimcp" and the command again.  On other systems get the
value with ":echo &rtp" in your ViAI.

==============================================================================
4. Tools					*viaimcp-tools*

						*viaimcp-viai_help_search*
viai_help_search {pattern}
		Lists the help tags that match the Vim regular expression
		{pattern}, with the help file each is in, at most 50.  The
		tags are those of the "doc/tags" files in 'runtimepath'.

						*viaimcp-viai_help_read*
viai_help_read {tag}
		Returns the help text of {tag}: from the line of the tag to
		the line before the next tag that follows an empty line.  For
		the tag of a section heading, after a line of "=", it is the
		whole section, and for the tag of a help file, such as
		"channel.txt", the whole file.  At most 300 lines are
		returned.  The first line is the help file and the line
		number where the text starts.  {tag} is matched exactly.

						*viaimcp-viai_vimscript_check*
viai_vimscript_check {path}
viai_vimscript_check {source}
		Checks a Vim script without running it: another ViAI reads it
		with ":source ++dryrun", see |:source-dryrun|, and the errors
		it reports are returned, or "No errors found".  Only the
		definitions take effect: other commands at the script level
		are not run or checked.  To check Vim9 script commands, put
		them in a |:def| function.  Give either {path}, the file of
		the script, or {source}, the text of the script.  For {source}
		the name of the script in the errors is "<source>"; a relative
		"import" in it is not found.

A tool that cannot do its work returns the reason with "isError" set: an
argument missing or of the wrong type, an invalid pattern, a tag or a file
that is not found.

==============================================================================
5. Development					*viaimcp-development*

The tests are in test/.  They start the server with the ViAI that runs
them: >
	test/run
	VIMPROG=/path/to/viai test/run
	TEST_FILTER=help test/run
<
 vim:tw=78:ts=8:noet:ft=help:norl:
